newsitem.title: GERMANY: Regional Airlines buys Deutsche BA aircraft.
newsitem.headline: Regional Airlines buys Deutsche BA aircraft.

text.p: French carrier Regional Airlines said it will buy five Saab 2000 turboprop aircraft from Deutsche BA as part of its expansion into Germany.
Regional Airlines, based at Nantes in western France, will take over the aircraft and a new subsidiary will operate the German regional routes of Deutsche BA from January 1, a company statement said.
Deutsche BA currently flies 10 domestic and international regional services out of Stuttgart, Friedrichshafen and Bremen.
But the loss-making British Airways subsidiary is dropping its regional turboprop network to expand its inner-German jet services routes.

Regional Airlines (Deutschland) GmbH, in which Regional Airlines will hold a 49 percent stake, aimed to carry 170,000 passengers and generate a turnover of 70 million marks in 1997, the statement said.
A private German investor will hold the remaining 51 percent, it added.
The new French-managed airline would be based at Stuttgart and have a staff of 120.

Through the additional Germany business, Regional Airlines aimed to fly 665,000 passengers and generate turnover of 900 million French frances in 1997, the statement added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
